title: Multiscale Light-Matter Dynamics in Quantum Materials: From Electrons to Topological Superlattices
problem: Simulating multiscale light-matter dynamics in topological quantum materials requires solving coupled Maxwell-Ehrenfest-surface hopping equations over vast spatiotemporal scales (15.4 million electrons, 1.23 trillion atoms). Traditional approaches face challenges: hardware heterogeneity (CPUs/GPUs), low-precision arithmetic limitations, and communication bottlenecks.
motivation: Light-induced control of topological properties enables ultralow-power, ultrafast quantum devices, but simulation at exascale requires new algorithmic and implementation strategies exploiting hardware diversity and reduced precision.
method: DC-MESH (divide-conquer-mesh) paradigm dividing multiscale/multiphysics problems into spatial and physical subproblems with small dynamic ranges and minimal mutual information. Subproblems mapped onto hardware best-matching characteristics (CPUs, GPUs, specialized units). Metamodel-space algebra minimizes communication and precision requirements. Implemented across 60,000 Aurora GPUs using XS-NNQMD (excited-state neural-network quantum molecular dynamics) and DC-MESH modules.
key_novelty: Divide-conquer-recombine multiphysics strategy with hardware-heterogeneity exploitation; metamodel-space algebra reducing communication and precision; neural-network quantum molecular dynamics at exascale.
contributions: DC-MESH algorithm for multiscale quantum materials simulation
XS-NNQMD neural-network quantum molecular dynamics module
limitations: Accuracy vs. precision trade-offs not detailed
Communication reduction mechanisms not fully specified
Applicability to other quantum materials unclear
